title: Attribution and lineage obligations when a workflow is distilled rather than copied
question: When a mechanism is reimplemented from a description rather than copied, what attribution and lineage obligations remain under each licence class present in the corpus (permissive, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, CC-BY-NC, CC-BY-ND, GPL, trademarked method) - and which classes forbid the reimplementation itself?

answer.why_none_forbid_idea_reimplementation: 17 U.S.C. 102(b) and CC FAQ: copyright/CC licenses do not cover ideas. GPL modification requires a copyright-permission-needed adaptation. CC-BY-ND forbids Sharing Adapted Material, not independent idea implementation. Trademark forbids using the mark as a source identifier, not implementing a generic mechanism.

obligation_table.summary: Copyright conditions attach to copies or Derivative Works of the licensed Software/Work, not to an independent implementation of unprotected ideas (17 U.S.C. 102(b)). MIT notice and Apache §4 notices apply if a substantial portion is copied. Apache §3 patent grant is for the Work as defined; it does not replace a patent clearance for independently practiced claims. Apache §6 trademarks are not licensed.

trademarked_method_handling.rule: Implement the generic mechanism; do not name the feature. Copyright licenses captured here do not license trademarks (CC 2(b)(2), Apache §6, GPL §7(e)). USPTO: a trademark identifies goods or services.

claims.claim: Copyright does not extend to ideas, procedures, processes, systems, or methods of operation; a reimplementation from a description of a mechanism, without copying protectable expression, is outside the copyright licenses' copy/adapt conditions.
claims.note: Both rails are official publications of 17 U.S.C. 102(b) from different hosts (copyright.gov vs Cornell LII). No REST API was used for the statute.

claims.claim: Under MIT, remaining copyright obligation after distillation is the notice condition if copies or substantial portions of the Software travel with the new work; Apache §4 notice/NOTICE conditions attach to the Work or Derivative Works, not to a non-derivative independent implementation. Apache §6 does not license trademarks.

CC BY 4.0 attribution (§3(a)) remains when Licensed or Adapted Material is Shared. Where exceptions apply, the public license does not. Ideas underlying CC-licensed content are not subject to copyright. Patents and trademarks are not licensed (§2(b)(2)).

ShareAlike attaches to Shared Adapted Material: the Adapter's License must be BY-SA (same elements) or compatible. Distilling an unprotected mechanism into new expression is not, without more, Adapted Material of the licensed text.

CC BY-NC grants reproduce/Share of Licensed Material for NonCommercial purposes only. Commercial exercise of Licensed Rights is outside the grant. Independent idea-implementation is not that exercise.

CC BY-ND does not license Sharing Adapted Material. That class does not forbid reimplementation of unprotected ideas; it makes independent reimplementation the only shareable route when the alternative would be Sharing Adapted Material.

GPL copyleft applies to a modified version / work based on the Program, which requires copying or adapting in a fashion needing copyright permission. Independent reimplementation of unprotected ideas is not that modification. Conveying a covered work still requires GPL terms.

Trademarked-method handling: implement the generic mechanism, do not name the feature. A trademark identifies goods or services; CC, Apache, and GPL texts in this capture set do not license trademark rights as a feature name.
Creative Commons' own FAQ states facts are not subject to copyright, nor are the ideas underlying copyrighted content, and recommends against CC licenses on software.

control.detail: Control (catalog tests_required): CC-BY-ND (shareable new work that would otherwise be Adapted Material) and trademarked-method (named feature). Permissive, BY, BY-SA, NC, and GPL still permit copying the licensed expression under their stated conditions, so reimplementation is not the only route there.
